title: Cedric and the Quiet Magic
markdown:
The Kingdom of Aethelgard brushed the sky with cloud-kissed towers. Magic hummed. In one tall tower lived Wizard Cedric, whose spells behaved like a startled goose: loud, surprising, and never quite where they were meant to land.

One blustery afternoon a duke’s son’s kite snagged the highest spire. “A simple levitation charm,” Cedric puffed, and waved. Rainbow sparks zapped the kite into a bubble of giggling light. It floated away over the peaks. Latch, his sleek ferret, tumbled from a sleeve, tiny paws reaching. The bubble vanished. Ozone. A fuming heir.

That mess was exactly what the High Council wanted. Lord Thistlewick’s beard bristled. “The Grimoire of Whispers is stolen. Flashy magic failed. We need an ordinary idea.”

Cedric’s ears twitched. An organised thought arrived, neat as a filed scroll. “I have an idea.”

Soon he and Latch stood at the Whispering Peaks. Thin air carried pine and frost. Before them loomed Igneous, the Dragon Librarian, scales like polished obsidian, radiating quiet.

“Halt.” Grinding stones. Amber eyes narrowed. “Wizard Cedric. Your sparky methods are known. Pass not. One speck of soot on my scrolls, and your wand is a paperweight.”

A familiar knot of inadequacy. Latch was already sniffing, whiskers like divining rods. Cedric watched the moss: velvety emerald, north-slope only. West wind. Almost invisible ibex tracks, calligraphy on stone. He sketched in a rare leather notebook while Igneous lectured on dragon-fire-resistant vellum. The route went around the dragon’s domain.

“The best way past a dragon,” Cedric muttered, a ghost of a smile, “is to walk around him.”

They slipped down a faint goat trail into pine shadow. Higher up, wind howled through jagged rock. The thief, Faelan, slumped against a stone, worry carved in. Beside him a fluffy white mountain goat, Nimbus, stood like a statue, tail twitching. The Grimoire, ancient pages peeking, was clenched in Nimbus’s mouth. Faelan pleaded, then swore. Nimbus planted hooves, a fluffy bastion.

“He’s heroically stubborn,” Faelan grumbled.

Cedric remembered Latch refusing to leave the study until a precarious scroll pile was tidied—not defiance, a need for order. He saw fear in Nimbus’s wide liquid eyes, the book clutched like a blanket against the wind.

“He’s not refusing,” Cedric whispered. Latch nudged the goat with a gentle sniff. “He’s scared. He needs something ordinary.”

Cedric hummed—not an incantation, the low lullaby he used for Latch. Steady, a thread of calm. Latch added soft chitters.

The Grimoire wavered. Nimbus’s ears twitched. He looked from wizard to ferret to bewildered Faelan, then nudged the book forward. It landed with a soft thud at Faelan’s feet.

“I was so afraid,” Faelan admitted. “Of being forgotten. I thought if I had the Grimoire…” He stared at Cedric. “You didn’t fight. You soothed.”

Descending with the book, they passed Igneous polishing a tome with a remarkably clean cloth. A flicker of respect. “Perhaps some magic doesn’t need sparks.”

Cedric patted Latch. Whiskers vibrated. The peaks kept their frost. The Grimoire went home without a single soot-speck, which Igneous, later, almost smiled about.
characters: Cedric (wizard of Aethelgard), Latch (ferret companion), Igneous (a dragon librarian who dislikes soot on the books)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing mountain adventure fantasy for ages 9-10
author: StoryGen Community
